subject.title: openai-responses transport sends null content, rejected by strict providers (400 schema error)

question: Should maintainers accept SDK strict-mock plus lifecycle regression proof as sufficient for a narrow `content: null` sanitizer, or require a live strict-provider repro before any fix lands?
rationale: The code path and prior PR show a plausible narrow fix, but the exact live weelinking history shape is not reproduced and the previous PR closed specifically because live proof was unavailable.

options.title: Accept strict-mock proof and sponsor a narrow sanitizer
options.body: Treat the prior SDK/lifecycle proof as enough for this wire-shape bug and reopen or recreate a focused fix that sanitizes all Responses send boundaries.

options.title: Require live strict-provider proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open as a watchlist until the reporter or a maintainer with provider access captures redacted logs from a real strict endpoint.

options.title: Reject runtime normalization
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide malformed `content: null` should be repaired earlier in transcript/session handling rather than tolerated at the transport boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept strict-mock proof and sponsor a narrow sanitizer
recommendation.body: Treat the prior SDK/lifecycle proof as enough for this wire-shape bug and reopen or recreate a focused fix that sanitizes all Responses send boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: The current send-boundary code blames to recent work by Peter Steinberger, and the decision is about provider-transport proof and normalization policy rather than a contributor-only patch detail.
